identification: Papua New Guinea Sepik River style carved and painted wooden wall mask, ovoid face with ridged brow, cowrie-shell rosettes on cheeks, cowrie/shell teeth, projecting beaked chin, ochre/white/grey pigments, fibre hanging cord. Back is flat, evenly grey and edged with lashing holes. Looks like a late 20th century (1970s-90s) commercially made trade/tourist piece in a Sepik (Abelam/Iatmul-influenced) style rather than a field-collected ritual mask; this is a judgement from photos only, not confirmed. Facebook 'Collecting Oceanic Art' answers describe similar cowrie-eye Sepik masks as made for tourist sale.

viewing_check: Armitage estimate 150-250, current bid $70 (+22% premium = about $85). Eyeball the back and rim: is the wood heavy and old with use wear, or a clean workshop piece? Check for cracks, insect damage and loose cowries. 68 x 36 cm, light, easy to post. eBay AU prices for comparable Sepik masks are mostly A$40-235 over the last 2 years with the middle around A$100-150, steady rather than rising. Old field-collected ritual Sepik masks sell much higher at specialist auctions, but nothing here confirms age.
